name.description: Addon instance name (legacy: also used as type in older configs)
name.title: Name

AdminSection.description:
[admin] section — an app's initial admin account (ADR 056).

The platform generates the password once (CSPRNG, stable across redeploy),
resolves the email, injects a canonical ``HOP3_ADMIN_USER`` /
``HOP3_ADMIN_EMAIL`` / ``HOP3_ADMIN_PASSWORD`` triple into the app's runtime
env, records the credential (encrypted, retrievable via ``hop3 app
credentials``), and runs ``create`` once post-deploy to create the account.
The recipe maps the canonical vars to whatever its app expects.

create.description: Idempotent (create-if-absent) command run once post-deploy to create the account. Receives HOP3_ADMIN_USER/EMAIL/PASSWORD in its environment. Omit when the app bootstraps itself from those vars.
create.title: Create

email.description: Admin email: 'operator' -> the server's OPERATOR_EMAIL, or a literal address. Omit when the app needs no admin email.
email.title: Email

login.description: Which identifier the app's sign-in form takes. Only the recipe knows: BookStack authenticates by email while its username is just a display name, so an operator handed both credentials picks wrong and is rejected. Omit only when the app declares just one of them.
login.title: Login

password.description: How to generate the admin password. Always generated (never a literal), so no credential is committed to the recipe.

username.description: Login username; omit when the app keys admins by email.
username.title: Username

verify.description: Command proving the account actually exists, run right after `create` and required to exit 0. Needed because a bootstrap CLI can print an error and still exit 0 — Gitea and Forgejo reject the reserved name 'admin' exactly that way — so `create`'s exit status is not evidence the account was made. Without this Hop3 reports only that the command ran, never that the account exists.
verify.title: Verify

AdminSection.title: AdminSection

ignore.description: Gitignore-style patterns to exclude from the `hop3 deploy` upload, on top of Hop3's built-in defaults (ADR 046 §5). The canonical ignore mechanism — the `.hop3ignore` sidecar and the `ignore-file` pointer are removed.
ignore.title: Ignore

node-version.description: Per-app Node.js version (installed via nodeenv into the app's virtualenv). Use when the app requires a Node newer/older than the host's system Node. Maps to NODE_VERSION env var internally.
node-version.title: Node-Version

static-dir.description: Directory a static site serves (toolchain = 'static'), relative to the app root — e.g. 'site', 'html', 'dist'. The first-class, Procfile-free way to point a static app at its content; defaults to 'public' when unset.
static-dir.title: Static-Dir

ContextSection.description:
A single ``[contexts.<name>]`` block — one deploy environment (ADR 042 r2).

A "context" is a (server, app, domains, env) bundle answering "where does
*this* project go for environment ``<name>``?". Multiple contexts express the
dev / staging / prod story for one codebase. Carries NO secrets: ``server``
is a literal address (the token lives in the CLI's per-server store), and a
committed-credential tripwire rejects secret-shaped values. Resolved
CLIENT-SIDE; the deployer ignores ``[contexts.*]``.

app.description: App instance name for this environment; inherits [metadata].id when absent.
app.title: App

domains.description: Hostnames for this environment — same shape as top-level [domains] (a `list = [...]` table). Full-replaces top-level when present.

env.description: Non-secret env overrides; merge over top-level [env]. Secrets go server-side via `hop3 env set`, never here.
env.title: Env

server.description: Literal address of the target Hop3 instance, e.g. ssh://root@prod.example.com. Never a symbolic name, never credentials.
server.title: Server

ContextSection.title: ContextSection

allow-http.description: Serve the app over plain HTTP as well as HTTPS. Off by default: Hop3 redirects HTTP to HTTPS, because an app told it is served over HTTPS issues Secure session/CSRF cookies that a browser will not send back over HTTP — logins then fail with no usable error. Enable only for an app that must answer on HTTP (the ACME challenge path stays on HTTP either way).
allow-http.title: Allow-Http

deployer.description: Force a specific deployer instead of auto-selecting by artifact kind: 'uwsgi', 'static', 'docker-compose', or 'auto' (default). Unknown names are rejected at deploy time against the installed deployers.
deployer.title: Deployer

DomainsSection.description:
[domains] section - First-class declaration of an app's hostnames.

Translates at deploy time into the HOST_NAME env var, which the reverse-
proxy plugins (nginx/caddy/traefik) read. Mirrors the [env] policy model:
by default values are treated as defaults (keep-existing); set
``_policy = "override"`` to update HOST_NAME on every deploy.

list.description: Hostnames to bind to this app, in declaration order.
list.title: List

DomainsSection.title: DomainsSection

EnvGenerate.description:
An `[env]` value the platform generates once on first deploy (ADR 046).

Replaces the per-app ``hop3 deploy --env KEY=$(...)`` workaround for apps
that need a secret/key to exist before first boot (Phoenix SECRET_KEY_BASE,
Laravel APP_KEY, Rails secret_key_base). The value is generated with a
CSPRNG when the var is unset, persisted as a normal app env var, and never
regenerated on redeploy (generated-once).

display.description: Surface the value once in deploy output (bootstrap creds).
display.title: Display

length.description: Entropy size: bytes for hex/base64/urlsafe, characters for password. Ignored for uuid. Per-generator default when omitted.
length.title: Length

prefix.description: Literal string prepended to the value (e.g. 'base64:').
prefix.title: Prefix

EnvGenerate.title: EnvGenerate

contains.description: Expected substring in the health-check response body. When set, the app counts as ready only once the endpoint returns a body containing it — a status-only 200 can be a placeholder, an error page, or another app's default_server content.
contains.title: Contains

retries.description: Number of retries before marking unhealthy
retries.title: Retries

LimitsSection.description:
[limits] section — per-app resource caps (ADR 046 §3).

A declared limit is a safety guarantee: if the platform can't enforce it the
deploy aborts rather than running an app that only *looks* capped. Today
enforcement is implemented for the Docker builder (compose mem_limit / cpus /
pids_limit); native/Nix enforcement needs cgroups via hop3-rootd and isn't
available yet, so [limits] on a non-Docker app fails loud at deploy.
LimitsSection.title: LimitsSection

MetadataSection.description: [metadata] section - Application identity and catalog info.
MetadataSection.title: MetadataSection

PortConfig.description: Port configuration for a single port (full format).

public.description: Whether the port is publicly accessible
public.title: Public

PortConfig.title: PortConfig

PortDeclaration.description:
A single [[ports]] entry — one fixed network port the app binds directly.

For non-HTTP services (SMTP, XMPP, RTMP, Matrix federation, …) there is no
reverse proxy or virtual hosting: the app binds the host port itself, so
exactly one app can own a given (number, protocol) on the host. Declaring
it lets Hop3 register the claim, refuse a conflicting second app up front,
and open/close the firewall for it. The HTTP port stays dynamic (``$PORT``,
proxied by nginx) and must NOT be declared here.

source.description: Who may reach the port: 'any' (the whole internet, default) or an IPv4 CIDR (e.g. '10.0.0.0/8') to restrict it to a network. IPv6 sources are not supported yet.
source.title: Source

PortDeclaration.title: PortDeclaration

ProbeSection.description:
[probe] section — a Hop3-owned account used to verify the app keeps working.

The [admin] credential is handed to the operator, so Hop3 stops owning it the
moment they change the password: a later sign-in failure could equally mean
the app broke or the password moved, and from outside those are the same
observation. A probe account nobody else uses removes that ambiguity — its
password is Hop3's to rotate, so a failed probe sign-in means the app broke.

It exists to exercise the FULL dynamic path — app code, session, database,
password verification — which no unauthenticated request reaches: a login
page renders fine with a dead database, and may not even be dynamic.

Deliberately NOT an administrator: signing in is the entire diagnostic value,
and a plain account carries a fraction of the privilege. Omit the section
entirely for an app whose data is sensitive enough that no standing Hop3
account is acceptable — the check then verifies the handover only, and says
so rather than silently testing less.

create.description: REQUIRED. Idempotent (create-if-absent) command that creates the account. Receives HOP3_PROBE_USER/EMAIL/PASSWORD in its environment, runs after the app is up, and must exit non-zero if the account does not end up existing.
create.title: Create

email.description: Email for the probe account, when the app requires one. A literal address; unlike [admin].email this is never the operator's, since the account is Hop3's and receives nothing.
email.title: Email

username.description: Login name for the probe account. Avoid names an app reserves (Gitea and Forgejo reject 'admin', while still exiting 0).
username.title: Username

verify.description: Command proving the probe account exists, run after `create` and required to exit 0. `create` is documented as having to exit non-zero on failure, but that is a promise the app's own CLI makes and some break it (Gitea and Forgejo print an error and exit 0 for the reserved name 'admin'). Declare this and the 'account exists' marker rests on evidence rather than on an app keeping that promise.
verify.title: Verify

ProbeSection.title: ProbeSection

before-run.description: Commands to run before starting the app
before-run.title: Before-Run

start.description: Start command for the web process
start.title: Start

start-timeout.description: Maximum time to wait for app to start (seconds)
start-timeout.title: Start-Timeout

static.description: Static file path mappings (URL path -> filesystem path)
static.title: Static

workers.description: Named worker processes (worker, scheduler, cron, etc.)
workers.title: Workers

TestSection.description:
[test] section — test-harness-specific fields.

Everything the test harness needs that cannot be derived from the rest
of hop3.toml. Fields like name / description / category / services /
deployment type are derived (from metadata, build.builder, addons).

Replaces the separate `test.toml` file — one source of truth per app.

covers.description: Free-form tags listing what the test exercises.
covers.title: Covers

expects-failure.description: Negative test case: the deploy is expected to fail. The runner treats a failed deploy as PASS and an unexpected successful deploy as FAIL. Used for ADR 039 Python-toolchain rejection paths and similar intentional-failure fixtures.
expects-failure.title: Expects-Failure

priority.description: Test priority: 'P0' | 'P1' | 'P2'. Selects which profile runs it.
priority.title: Priority

tier.description: Test-tier label, used in reports only (no longer drives any timeout). Values: 'fast' | 'medium' | 'slow' | 'very-slow'.
tier.title: Tier

validations.description: HTTP checks beyond the single [healthcheck] endpoint.
validations.title: Validations

TestSection.title: TestSection

TestValidation.description:
A single [[test.validations]] entry — one HTTP check the test harness
performs after the app is up.

contains.description: If set, response body must contain this substring.
contains.title: Contains

status-in.description: Accept any of these status codes. Useful for apps whose first-boot install wizard legitimately returns 202 before migrations complete (e.g., xwiki). When set, `status` is ignored.
status-in.title: Status-In

type.description: Validation type. Currently only 'http' is supported.
type.title: Type

TestValidation.title: TestValidation

VolumeBackupSection.description:
`[volumes.backup]` — per-volume backup policy (ADR 046 §2/§4a).

A strict table so a typo (e.g. ``inclide = false``) is rejected at deploy
time rather than silently leaving the volume in the backup. ``include``
(default true) is the only key acted on today.

include.description: Whether this volume's data is captured by `hop3 backup create`.
include.title: Include

VolumeBackupSection.title: VolumeBackupSection

VolumeSection.description:
A `[[volumes]]` entry — a path that survives the source-replacing redeploy.

``persist`` (the default, and the only implemented type) links ``target`` —
a directory inside the app's source tree — to storage under the app's data
root (`<app>/volumes/<name>/`), so writes outlive the redeploy that wipes
`src/`.

backup.description: Per-volume backup policy; omit to include the volume in backups.

mode.description: Octal permissions for the volume directory.
mode.title: Mode

name.description: Logical volume name; storage lives at <app>/volumes/<name>.
name.title: Name

size.description: Size cap for a tmpfs volume (e.g. '256M').
size.title: Size

target.description: Directory inside the app tree to back with the volume (relative).
target.title: Target

VolumeSection.title: VolumeSection

threshold.description: Violations within the window before a ban.
threshold.title: Threshold

WafGate.description:
A ``[[waf.gate]]`` entry — conditional access (ADR 050 §2, use case 2).

Matching paths are reachable only when ``require`` holds. v1 supports a
named network (operator-defined, resolved at deploy from the DB); ``auth``
is reserved but rejected here until Hop3 forward-auth exists (ADR 050 §5 /
Security invariant — fail loud, never a silent allow).

require.description: Condition: a named network (v1), or 'auth' (deferred — rejected).
require.title: Require

WafGate.title: WafGate

WafSection.description:
The ``[waf]`` section — per-app Layer-7 WAF policy (ADR 050).

Two access constructs (ADR 050 §2): ``allow`` (a positive allowlist that, when
present, denies everything else — use case 1) and ``[[waf.gate]]`` (conditional
access — use case 2). ``[[waf.tuning]]`` relaxes CRS false positives; ``[waf.bans]``
throttles repeat offenders. Off by default (``enabled = false``).

allow.description: Positive model: URL-path regexes the app serves. If present, any path matching none of these (and no satisfied gate) is denied.
allow.title: Allow

WafSection.title: WafSection

WafTuning.description:
A ``[[waf.tuning]]`` entry — scoped CRS false-positive relief (ADR 050 §3).

Verb-named keys (``disable-rule-ids`` / ``skip-body-inspection``) so the
direction is unambiguous (never the old "exclusions"). Scoped to ``paths``;
omit ``paths`` for a global entry.

disable-rule-ids.description: CRS rule IDs to turn off (within the scope).
disable-rule-ids.title: Disable-Rule-Ids

paths.description: Path regexes to scope this tuning to; omit for global.
paths.title: Paths

reason.description: Why the relief is needed — surfaced for audit.
reason.title: Reason

skip-body-inspection.description: Don't scan request bodies (within the scope).
skip-body-inspection.title: Skip-Body-Inspection

WafTuning.title: WafTuning

description: Configuration for a Hop3 application. Generated from the server's own validation models; cross-field rules are enforced at deploy time.

admin.description: Initial admin account to bootstrap on first deploy (ADR 056). The platform generates the password, creates the account, and surfaces the credential to the operator.

contexts.description: Per-project deploy environments (ADR 042, 2nd revision). Each [contexts.<name>] bundles (server, app, domains, env) for one environment — dev/staging/prod. Non-secret; resolved client-side; ignored by the deployer.
contexts.title: Contexts

domains.description: App hostnames. Translates to HOST_NAME at deploy time. Mutually exclusive with setting HOST_NAME under [env].

env.description: Environment variables. Set _policy = 'override' to update existing values on redeploy.
env.title: Env

limits.description: Per-app resource caps (ADR 046 §3): memory / cpu / processes. Enforced for Docker apps; declaring them on a non-Docker app fails loud until cgroup enforcement lands.

nix.description: Nix template configuration for auto-generating hop3.nix. Requires [nix].template to be set. See ADR 008.
nix.title: Nix

ports.description: Fixed host ports the app binds directly (non-HTTP services: SMTP, XMPP, RTMP, Matrix federation, …). Each is claimed exclusively on the host; a second app declaring the same port is refused before deploy. The HTTP port stays dynamic ($PORT, proxied) — don't list it here.
ports.title: Ports

probe.description: A Hop3-owned account for verifying the app keeps working, whose password Hop3 controls (see ProbeSection).

static.description: Static file path mappings (URL path -> filesystem path)
static.title: Static

test.description: Test-harness metadata. Replaces the separate test.toml file — see TestSection for fields.

volumes.description: Declarative persistent volumes (ADR 046 §2). Each links a directory in the app tree to storage that survives the source-replacing redeploy.
volumes.title: Volumes

waf.description: Layer-7 Web Application Firewall policy (ADR 050): positive allowlist / conditional gates, CRS tuning, and bans. Off unless [waf].enabled = true.

title: hop3.toml
